title: Man fatally shot by Edmonton police was armed with two knives, police watchdog says
subtitle: The 26-year-old man was shot several times Wednesday night during a confrontation with Edmonton police outside a townhouse in the city's east end. The Alberta Serious Incident Response Team is investigating the incident.
article: A 26-year-old man who died after being shot by Edmonton police on Wednesday night was armed with two knives, according to new details released by the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT), the province's police watchdog, which has taken over the investigation.

Devlin Kyle Neyando died at the scene when officers opened fire outside a townhouse on the city's east side during a confrontation. Neyando was being sought by police after reports that a 28-year-old woman had been assaulted for several days at the same location.

According to ASIRT, the police received a domestic violence call at around 1 p.m. related to Neyando, but he was not at the townhouse where the complainant lived. The woman was found with injuries and was taken to hospital, police said.
Later in the evening, at around 9 p.m., police received further reports that Neyando had broken inside the same home, while only a 13-year-old child was present. Police then responded to the scene.

As police approached the home, Neyando emerged from the front door with two knives in hand, according to ASIRT. The knives were obtained from inside the home. Neyando was then shot several times after a confrontation with two Edmonton Police Service members that resulted in his death. Non-lethal shots were also fired by police during the confrontation, ASIRT said.
It is unclear whether Neyando threatened the officers with the knives, or if any of the police members were hurt during the confrontation. An autopsy on Neyando was scheduled for Friday.

Neyando, who has lived in Edmonton since his teens and is originally from Fort McPherson in the Northwest Territories, was due to appear in Edmonton court on Jan. 23 on two charges of assault with a weapon.
Wednesday's fatal shooting was the second involving Edmonton police in about a week.

On Dec. 26, a 34-year-old man being sought on outstanding warrants died after police stopped a vehicle he was in. Police said they believed the man, identified by friends as Buck Evans, was armed and dangerous.
Both shootings are being investigated by ASIRT.
ASIRT investigates incidents involving Alberta's police that have resulted in serious injury or death to any person, as well as serious or sensitive allegations of police misconduct.
